citations.source_publication: Elsie Warnock, “Terms of Approbation and Eulogy in American Dialect Speech,” Dialect Notes, IV, part I
citations.source_archive: Internet Archive; University of Toronto copy
citations.verbatim_quote: doozy. Sporty, flossy. Facetious. Used in Nebraska. See DIALECT NOTES, III, 543. “Where’s that doozy fellow I saw you with?” “She’s a trifle bit doozy.”
citations.linguistic_note: Sporty or flossy; two adjectival examples
citations.analysis_notes: Displayed source is the dated Part I fascicle, not the 1917 bound volume. Warnock explicitly cites Pound’s p. 543, so the gloss does not count as a second independent discovery; her two sentences are additional usage examples without individual informant dates.
